When the average temperature exceeds 27 °C, the NOC operator moves the non-critical server load of server room B to another server room."},{"source_unit_id":"P5","text":"At 2:16 a.m., when the average temperature reaches 27.5 °C, the operator, in consultation with the customer support team, migrates the virtual machines of 80 non-critical servers to server room A, and at the same time turns off the lighting and humidifiers of server room B to reduce heat generation."},{"source_unit_id":"P6","text":"Virtual machine migration proceeds 10 servers at a time, and after each migration it is checked whether the service response time is 200 ms or less. If the response time exceeds the threshold, the operator stops the migration, identifies the cause, and then resumes."},{"source_unit_id":"P7","text":"At 2:18 a.m. CH-3 reached its rated capacity, and the average temperature fell below 25 °C at 2:30 a.m. Had the average temperature exceeded 30 °C, the operator would have started the planned shutdown procedure for the critical servers."},{"source_unit_id":"P8","text":"The facilities team, on receiving the NOC's call, arrives on site, inspects the CH-2 compressor, and confirms that the overcurrent relay has tripped. The team shares the symptoms with the manufacturer's remote support center via video call and receives a diagnosis of compressor motor winding damage."},{"source_unit_id":"P9","text":"Because a compressor with damaged windings cannot be repaired on site, the facilities team orders a replacement part from the manufacturer and marks CH-2 as inoperable until the part arrives. Part arrival takes about 3 days."},{"source_unit_id":"P10","text":"Since cooling must meanwhile be done with CH-1 and CH-3 only, the operator raises the setpoint temperature of server room B from 22 °C to 23 °C and establishes a contingency plan for the case where one more chiller stops."},{"source_unit_id":"P11","text":"According to the contingency plan, if only one chiller remains, the operator shuts down all non-critical servers in server room B, notifies the customers, and then keeps only the critical servers running.
